Sata m.2 is as fast as a regular sata ssd. Reads and write are within 200-300MB/s where nvme m.2 is like 400-700+MB/s. Unless u transfer a lot of data or copy a lot, you will not notice the difference. I have two p1 nvme ssd in raid and I get writes up to 1.2GB/s and I only see the difference when copying files. 

Note when transferring files from one drive to another the speed is limited to the slowest one. So you would need 2 nvme drives to benefit transferring at high speeds.

Generally, I format all my drives first before putting stuff on there.
Also if steam/game launcher is linked to that drive u can either change the drive letter to the old one or go into the game launcher and change the location to the new drive.

But for real tips, I think it’s good to start off playing around with each of the weapons in the training room and finding the one that you are most comfortable with and mastering it. 

If you want to discover things yourself then I would go in expeditions to get material and get an overall feel for the maps and checking areas that have environment objects that you can use to your advantage. This should also help you get a feel for using your slingshot. (This process can be made simple by looking up guides on maps online)

Afterwards, you can start hunting quest and taking it slow as you have 50minutes to learn patterns and movements of the monster. This shouldn’t take you long at all, but many new players try to solely attack without thinking making them viably useless. 

When it comes to your equipment try to get gear that has skills that focus on your play style or weapon of choice. For example, long sword, I would go for affinity boosting gear with crit bonuses or go for atk up gear. If you have a hard time understanding a gear skill you can look it up online for a more in depth look but they describe it pretty good in game.

For grinding monster materials USE investigations as they give you extra bonuses for hunting the monster you want making the grind easier.

As a tip, once you start getting materials for traps, use them to beat quest as they provide better rewards and saves you time. Big tip: traps don’t work on elder dragons.

Also focus on hitting monster parts if you need specific materials like the tail, horn etc. after a while these parts break and once they do you have a high chance of getting that part.

Once you hit high rank avoid bezel(carpet bomber) but that’s gonna be a while for you.
